name: Laggar Falcon
rangeDescription: Southeastern iran to india and myanmar
description: A large, slender falcon with long wings that nearly reach its tail tip when perched. It has a rusty crown above a thin white brow that can connect to its pale forecrown, above a bold dark eye-stripe that extends to the nape.

name: Ochre-collared Monarch
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northern new guinea, including yapen (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: A slender, medium-sized bird of lowland and foothill forest. Fairly long tail and black face with gray bill and blue eye wattle.

name: Sclater's Crowned-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Southern new guinea (mimika river to fly river)
description: An enormous pigeon of the southern lowland rainforests. Erect, mohicanlike crest is especially long at the back.

name: Sooty Ant-Tanager
rangeDescription: Northwestern colombia, from the northern end of the western andes (upper sinú valley) eastward along the northern base of the andes, and southward to both sides of the middle magdalena valley
description: Rather large, chunky tanager endemic to northwestern Colombia. Unlikely to be mistaken.

name: Sooty Grassquit
rangeDescription: Colombia to venezuela, guyana, and eastern and southwestern brazil
description: Small nondescript finchlike bird found at humid forest edges and in shrubby and grassy areas. Males are sooty black with a gray bill.

name: Visayan Pygmy-Babbler
rangeDescription: Philippines (leyte and samar)
description: A small bird of lowland and foothill forest and edge on Leyte and Samar, frequenting middle heights in the forest. Rufous-brown on the crown, back, wings, and tail, with a gray chest and a blackish throat and face, all with fine white streaking.

name: Buff-sided Robin
rangeDescription: Northern australia (fitzroy river, western australia to northwestern queensland)
description: Small round songbird found in heavy vegetation along creeks and thick wet forest, including bamboo clumps, of northern-central Australia. Brown above, pale below, with broad white supercilium, dark ear coverts, peachy-rufous flanks and undertail, and white markings in wing and tail.

name: Brown Parrotbill
rangeDescription: Bamboo forest of nepal to southeastern tibet, southwestern china, and northeastern myanmar
description: Dark brown parrotbill with a stout yellow bill and an arching black eyebrow. Like many other parrotbills, shows a strong affinity for high-elevation bamboo thickets, in which it moves about noisily in small flocks.

name: Levant Sparrowhawk
rangeDescription: Balkans to russia; winters to northeastern africa and arabian peninsula
description: Small, dark-eyed hawk of woodland, scrub, riparian corridors, and wooded plains and slopes. Note the adult's grayish upperparts and orange-barred underparts; females are larger and darker than males, with a dark central throat stripe.

name: White-chested Puffbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to eastern peru, the guianas, and western amazonian brazil
description: Brown-and-white streaked bird with a large head and yellowish bill; white crescent on chest is helpful for identification but can be difficult to see. Inhabits lower and middle levels of tall rainforest, where it is easily overlooked as it sits motionless for long periods before darting to tree trunks, foliage, or ground for large insect and small vertebrate prey.

name: Malaita Owl
rangeDescription: Malaita (central solomon islands)
description: A rather small dark brown owl with black eyes, a white throat, and white eyebrows. Underparts are densely barred.

name: Sri Lankan Shama
rangeDescription: Sri lanka
description: A thrushlike bird with a long, graduated tail, endemic to Sri Lanka. Males are glossy black above and orange below.

name: White-bellied Tanager
rangeDescription: Coastal southeastern brazil (southern bahia to rio de janeiro)
description: Endemic to southeastern Brazil. Striking tanager found in the canopy in forest, edges, plantations, and gardens.

name: Gray Falcon
rangeDescription: Sparse in arid and semiarid areas of australia with scattered trees
description: Seldom-seen pale gray falcon of inland Australia found in arid grassland and woodland habitats, where it sometimes perches high on communication towers. Pale gray upperparts and white underparts, with faint dark streaks below.

name: Black-chinned Yuhina
rangeDescription: Northern india eastward to central and southeastern china, southward to western myanmar, northern and central laos, vietnam, and far eastern cambodia
description: A small yuhina of open forest environments. Black chin is not very noticeable, but the black crest is.

name: Dwarf Vireo
rangeDescription: Arid highlands of southwestern mexico (southeastern jalisco to oaxaca)
description: Small, relatively active vireo of scrubby woodlands and brushy thickets in highlands; mainly in areas of oak woodland. Endemic to southwestern Mexico.

name: Laysan Finch
rangeDescription: Laysan island (northwestern hawaiian islands)
description: A finch-billed Hawaiian honeycreeper endemic to the island of Laysan; does not occur in the main Hawaiian Islands. An introduced population occurs on Pearl and Hermes Atoll.

name: Pygmy Cuckooshrike
rangeDescription: High montane forest of northern, central, and southeastern sulawesi
description: A distinctive small cuckooshrike with bright white underbody, a dusky gray upperside, and a prominent red eye. Males display a contrasting black face and chin, while females’ faces have the same gray color as the back.

name: Black-casqued Hornbill
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed forest of western and central africa; bioko island
description: A gigantic black hornbill of African rainforests, often seen or heard in the canopy feeding on fruiting trees. Undertakes seasonal movements, and can be surprisingly common at certain times of year and absent in others.

name: Salvin's Prion
rangeDescription: Breeds prince edward island and crozet island; at sea occurs in southern indian ocean and australasian seas
description: A pale powder-blue-and-white seabird with a faint grayish dark “M” across the upperwings. Note the dark blue “thumb mark” collar, the blue eye-stripe, the white eyebrow, the white throat, and the grayish cap.
